summary: Iteration 2 E2E testing for new Batch Processing and Automations (Webhook Drops) features. Backend: 17/17 pytest cases green (4 new: batch process + zip download, batch download 404, automations auth guard, full automation lifecycle + webhook drop + 404 after delete). Frontend: Batch tab renders with data-testids, multi-file upload works, POST /api/batch/process returns 2 processed files with valid ZIP download link. Automations tab renders correct auth-gate for anonymous users; after login and creating a recipe, create button enables, modal creates webhook, card shows public webhook URL + curl snippet, copy button works, delete confirms and removes card. runs_count increments after webhook drop (verified in backend test).

minor.issue: No storage_key persistence per processed_item is recorded in DB (Execution rows are not created for each batch item), unlike single-file /api/files/export. History view will miss batch runs.
Files with unsupported extensions are silently skipped (no error surfaced to caller). Better to include them in results with an 'error' field.
Sequential processing inside a single request loop — for large batches (10+ big files) will be slow. Feature name suggests 'concurrently'; consider asyncio.gather with polars in a thread pool.
No rate-limiting or auth on token; anyone with the token can trigger unlimited executions. Consider signed HMAC header or per-token throttling for production.
No PATCH endpoint to toggle is_active or rename an automation — only create/list/delete are exposed.

issues: Webhook URL box uses a fixed dark bg (#080D18) even in light theme, causing inconsistent look on light mode.
curl snippet block similarly hard-codes dark palette.
Native <select> elements used for recipe/format instead of shadcn Select components used elsewhere — slight inconsistency.

action_items: Optional: persist Execution rows for each batch-processed file so the History tab reflects batch runs.
Optional: return skipped/unsupported files with error info in /api/batch/process response instead of silent drop.
Optional: add lightweight auth (HMAC signature or per-token secret) and rate-limiting to /api/webhooks/drop/{token}.
Optional: expose PATCH /api/automations/{id} to toggle is_active and rename.
Optional (UI): theme-aware colors for webhook URL/curl snippet boxes in AutomationsView; migrate BatchProcessingView selects to shadcn Select for consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L604: batch_process wraps the whole loop in one zipfile.ZipFile 'w' context — good — but on parse errors mid-loop the endpoint will 500 instead of continuing; wrap each file in try/except and append error entries to results.

server.py L644: individual per-file storage_key is saved to disk but never referenced from the response beyond returning the key — no endpoint to fetch a single processed file, forcing users to unzip the batch archive.
server.py L757: AutomationWebhook.is_active is stored as Integer(1/0); comparing with `== 1` works but a Boolean column would be cleaner.

server.py L811: webhook_drop commits webhook.runs_count and recipe.execution_count in the same transaction as the Execution insert — good — but no error surface if content-type isn't multipart/form-data (FastAPI 422). Should return a clearer 400 message for API consumers.
Previous iteration notes still apply: FILE_CACHE in-memory dict, JWT_SECRET default fallback, and /api/samples still uses next(get_db()).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (batch upload+process+zip, automations auth-gate, create/list/copy/delete card)

seed_data_creation: During UI test seeded 'TEST_UI_Auto_Recipe' via API to enable the create-automation flow; deleted post-test. TEST_UI_Webhook automation created via UI and deleted via UI. Pytest fixtures create and clean 'TEST_ERP_Recipe', 'TEST_Auto_Recipe' and 'TEST_Webhook_ERP'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New endpoints /api/batch/process, /api/batch/download/{key}, /api/automations (POST/GET/DELETE), /api/webhooks/drop/{token} are all covered by pytest and Playwright. All flows green. The webhook token is public — a bad actor with the URL can execute recipes; consider adding auth. The demo account starts with no recipes after test cleanup, so 'Nuevo Webhook Drop' button will be disabled until a recipe is saved (this is correct behavior, guarded by amber warning banner).
